weak_points: The 'breathing slot' hook is subtle — risk of reading as just camera shake rather than an intentional inhale/exhale motion. Needs a clear contraction/expansion beat in frame 1.
Scene 2 (9s) wrongness beat could drag if the vault door reveal happens too late in the clip; want it visible by ~3s in.
stronger_hook: Open on the slot mid-contraction (already moving), not before it starts — viewer should catch it already happening, which reads as 'I'm seeing something I shouldn't' rather than 'something is about to happen.'
pacing_plan: Scene 1 (2s): no trim, hook stays tight.
Scene 2 (9s): trim to ~6-7s in final cut if the vault door is static after reveal; push remaining time into scene 3's corridor chase.
Scene 3 (8s): keep full duration, this carries the chase energy.
Scene 4 (8s): keep full duration; the guard's turn-and-freeze beat should land by the 2-3s mark of this scene, not at the very end.
Scene 5 (3s): no trim, abrupt cut to black on the empty pedestal.
subtitle_rewrite: My piggy bank's coin slot just breathed.
A vault door. Dented. Alarm spinning.
One froze. Looked straight at the slot.
Whatever they guarded is already gone.
audio_emphasis_plan: A soft inhale/exhale whoosh synced exactly to the slot's breathing motion in scene 1.
Alarm klaxon (low, distant, non-jarring) starting under scene 2's vault reveal.
Footsteps/scrambling texture under scene 3's corridor chase, cutting to dead silence the instant the guard freezes in scene 4.
A single heavy mechanical thud as lights cut to red at the start of scene 5.
retention_edit_instructions: Once footage exists: ffmpeg trim scene 2 if vault door reveal arrives late, never re-cut scene 1.
Hold scene 4 on the guard's freeze frame as long as possible without exceeding 8s — this is the most shareable single frame.
Burn subtitles per timing above; keep 'At me.' isolated as its own short beat for maximum unease.
